Patient demographics:
  age: 60
  gender: Male
  ethnicity: South Eastern Asian
  relationship_status: Married
  occupation: Fisherman
  trauma_type: Trauma to a loved one
  pcl5: 40

Patient-reported symptoms:
  Threat: Physical Reactivity: Having strong physical reactions when something reminded you of the stressful experience, Negative Emotions: Having strong negative feelings such as fear, horror, anger, guilt, or shame, Sleep Problems: Trouble falling or staying asleep
  Negative Appraisals: Mistrust: People can't be trusted, Emotional Numbness: I feel dead inside, Survival Guilt: I feel guilty for surviving when others did not

Vignette:
Mr. Nguyen is a 60-year-old married man of South Eastern Asian descent who has been a fisherman for over three decades. He and his wife have always led a simple life, spending most of their time at sea or in their small coastal community. Tragically, Mr. Nguyen’s world was turned upside down when he witnessed the loss of his younger brother during a fishing expedition a year ago. The incident occurred on what seemed like another ordinary day at work. As they were navigating through stormy waters, a sudden wave capsized their boat. Despite their best efforts to stay afloat and call for help, Mr. Nguyen watched in horror as his brother was swept away by the turbulent sea. The memory of that fateful day has left him with strong physical reactions whenever he encounters reminders of the traumatic event. Mr. Nguyen’s daily life now is punctuated by heightened arousal and anxiety. Even the gentle hum of a motorboat or the sound of crashing waves can send his heart racing and trigger a cascade of panic. He often experiences an overwhelming sense of fear, horror, and guilt. The thought that he could have done more to save his brother haunts him relentlessly. In the weeks following the accident, Mr. Nguyen’s sleep became severely disrupted. Nightmares of the incident replayed in his mind each night, making it almost impossible for him to get a full night's rest. He would often find himself waking up drenched in sweat and struggling to calm down before he could fall back asleep. Mr. Nguyen had come to believe that people cannot be trusted. The unpredictability of life at sea had made him increasingly wary of others, finding it hard to open up or rely on his colleagues. This mistrust has strained his relationships with fellow fishermen who once shared a camaraderie and support system. Furthermore, he often felt emotionally numb and disconnected from the world around him. Even simple pleasures like spending time with his family no longer brought joy; instead, they were overshadowed by the constant weight of guilt for surviving while others did not. This emotional numbing has also affected his ability to engage in daily tasks, making it difficult for him to focus on his work. Over time, these symptoms have compounded and affected Mr. Nguyen’s life significantly. He began avoiding activities that reminded him of the traumatic event, such as going out to sea or even talking about what happened with his family. This avoidance led to a noticeable decline in his fishing trips, affecting his income and contributing to further financial stress. What frightened him most was the sense of isolation and detachment from those around him. He felt like an outsider, unable to connect emotionally with others due to the overwhelming burden he carried. The cumulative impact of these experiences eventually became too much for him to bear alone. It was a particularly tough day at home that finally pushed Mr. Nguyen to seek help. His wife had noticed his increasing withdrawal and the toll it was taking on their relationship, urging him to talk to someone who could provide support and guidance. He is now seeking therapy to address these symptoms and hopes to find a way to reconnect with those around him and regain some semblance of peace. Mr. Nguyen’s current state reflects a deep-seated fear of not being able to cope with the pain and guilt associated with his brother's death, while also harboring a strong desire to heal and move forward. He is most hoping for relief from the overwhelming physical reactions, emotional numbness, and negative emotions that have dominated his life since the accident.
